SYSTEMATIC GAPS, confirmed by my all-blob passes over all 307 mirrors. Pass 1 was a credential-shape scan of 138,244 blobs (3.94 GB), reading raw bytes plus 91 zips and 906 gzip streams decoded in memory. Pass 2 read binary metadata. With default settings, neither gitleaks nor the sweep's text layers see secrets inside zip or tar.gz (Terraform plans, backups), inside .pyc bytecode, or inside PDFs. Every new credential in this report sits in one of those. Pass 2 found no EXIF GPS in any JPEG. It found home paths in: pyc files (agenttool-sdk-py, 11 in HEAD, which the batch already says to drop; agent-memory, 12 in history; rhetorlint-spec, 1 in history; yutabase, a HEAD pyc that includes this machine's account name); Mach-O binaries (zerone-* and AxiePro history); and the research PDFs. Before anything is published, re-run the sweep with archive and bytecode decoding, and add a Codeberg/userinfo rule.

METHOD. Read-only throughout. I made no push and changed no setting. No repo code was executed. Python ran with -I, and all scripts and outputs are outside mirrors/, under oss-audit/critic/ in the session scratchpad named in the task: tools/credscan.py, tools/binscan.py, tools/ctxinspect.py, tools/sg.py, credscan/*.jsonl and binscan/*.json (sha256 prefixes, shapes and masked paths only, never values), and cred_agg.json. GitHub: about 240 GETs (core 4,747 remaining at the end), covering the private and public repo lists, commit-existence checks of private root commits against public twins, the first 100 commits of each public repo, root listings of each public repo, and 3 hook-blob comparisons. All 'live' judgements are shape-based; I tested no credential and probed no service.

LIMITS. My regexes cover about 20 key families plus generic assignments and URL userinfo; secrets with no prefix (Cloudflare global keys, 32-hex vendor keys) were not hunted. The public-twin check compares only the newest 100 commits of each public repo, plus root-commit tests for 21 name pairs. I did not check the content of public repos beyond root listings and 3 hook blobs, nor whether the zerone dashboard serves the research PDFs. My verdict-consistency checks rest on rule-hit profiles and the batch text, not on full re-reads.

SLIPS, said plainly: one context view printed the 8-character tail of an AWS access key ID (an identifier, not the secret) in my local output before I widened the mask; one masked grep printed two retired server IP addresses from Love's security notes; and I compared an address against the local global git config inside code without printing it.
